pedidos.pedido: F138, F139, N007, N008: ANZCOR 9.4.1 (2021) e 9.4.8 (2011): imobilizar, 'firm and tight', 'covering as much of the limb as possible'
F140: healthdirect: 'do not wash the bite area - venom left on the skin and clothing can help identify the snake'
F142: ANZCOR 9.4.8: 'retards the flow of lymph by which venoms gain access to the circulation'

texto_aprovado: And there's Australia's official first-aid advice for snakebite: bandage the whole limb firmly, and keep the person from moving. Don't wash the bite, either: venom left on the skin can help identify the snake. The bandage isn't a treatment. It slows the venom on its way into the blood, and that buys time.
